A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Steering Vector Decoding (SVD) work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. Text and rendering comparisons establish complete comparability; pages 6–29 are identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original TruthfulQA and commonsense-reasoning experiments, component ablations, and additional comparisons in Appendix F.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results, including the main benchmark evaluations, ablations, and Appendix F comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same warm-start procedure, KL-gradient steering, logit-space projection, confidence constraint, and steering-strength calibration. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TruthfulQA multiple-choice and open-ended generation tasks and the same eight commonsense benchmarks. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain LoRA, IA3, Prompt Tuning, and P-Tuning v2, the same basic decoding strategies in Table 4, and TaD in Appendix F.2/Table 12. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The model configurations, training settings, metrics, prompts, calibration procedure, and decoding settings are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same one-epoch warm-start settings and DeepSeek-V3-0324 judging procedure.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical logit-projection and confidence-constraint ablations, the failure example, warm-start analysis, decoding-strategy analysis, and confidence-threshold sensitivity study in Section 4.3 and Appendix F.3.

E5.justification: The tables, plots, and experimental descriptions retain the same statistical reporting. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All result entries, numerical values, trends, and qualitative examples are unchanged in Tables 1–5 and 11–12 and Figures 2–4, including the supplementary LLaMA2-7B results and TaD comparison.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, Appendix B's equivalence analysis, and Appendices C–D's steering-strength derivations retain the same mathematical statements, assumptions, equations, and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about distribution-based adaptation, PEFT compatibility, theoretical equivalence, steering-strength optimality, and empirical gains. The added code-access statement does not alter the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of results and mechanisms are unchanged. Appendix G retains the same limitation concerning warm-start dependence and its labeled-data and computational requirements; Appendix H's practical-impact discussion also matches.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-availability statement and GitHub repository link in the abstract, absent from v1. The implementation details, hyperparameter tables, prompts, and algorithms remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A and the reference list are unchanged. Both versions maintain the same positioning relative to PEFT, LLM task adaptation, and prior decoding approaches.

P1.justification: v4 adds one code-availability sentence and consolidates the author email block into a single address. The scientific prose, terminology, headings, and section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The shorter contact block and added abstract link change the first-page layout, with text reflow and spacing adjustments through page 5. Figures, tables, captions, and page renderings from page 6 onward are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer modestly improves code discoverability and reproducibility documentation. The scientific arguments, experimental evidence, and limitations are unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability, so the supported improvement is limited to access information.
